title: pdf_prebake.gleam imports four unused items and defines an unused helper
evidence: import application/sql.{ type GetApplicationDetailRow, type GetCoApplicantsByApplicationRow, type GetDocumentsByApplicationRow, type GetIncomeSourcesByApplicationRow, GetApplicationDetailRow, } ... import gleam/result ... fn str_opt(value: String) -> Option(String) { case value { "" -> None s -> Some(s) } }
detail: Full-file grep shows GetCoApplicantsByApplicationRow, GetDocumentsByApplicationRow, GetIncomeSourcesByApplicationRow, gleam/result and str_opt appear only at their import/definition lines — never referenced. The snapshot is built with empty lists (co_applicants: [], income_sources: [], documents: []), so the types were imported for a richer snapshot that wasn't shipped. Gleam emits unused-import warnings; build is plain `gleam build` (no warnings-as-errors), so CI stays green.
recommended_fix: Drop the four unused imports and the unused str_opt function, or actually populate co_applicants/income_sources/documents so the imported types are used.

title: pdf_prebake main() ignores the documented priv-dir argument
evidence: //// Regenerate (after fixture craft changes): ////   gleam run -m demo/pdf_prebake -- server/priv ////   (cwd = server/; the arg is the priv dir. Defaults to "priv" relative to the server package root.) ... pub fn main() { let priv_dir = "priv"
detail: The header instructs running with `-- server/priv` and says the arg is the priv dir, but main() hardcodes `let priv_dir = "priv"` and never reads argv. The documented invocation silently ignores its argument; output always lands in <cwd>/priv/static/demo/. Harmless from server/ (as documented), misleading from any other cwd.
recommended_fix: Read the argv arg (or drop the `-- server/priv` from the doc comment and keep priv hardcoded to the server package root).

title: CI demo-mode lint pins rsvp/api_helpers primitives but not imports of the real api modules
evidence: VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rn "rsvp\|api_helpers" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true) ... FETCH_VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rln "gleam/fetch" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" | grep -v "demo_api.gleam" || true)
detail: Every real api module imports rsvp (verified: all 10 client/src/api/* modules match), but a demo module importing `import api/vacancy_api` functions directly would contain neither banned string and pass the lint — the actual network seam is unpinned. Not vacuous today (demo/ has no rsvp/api_helpers/gleam-fetch except the documented demo_api.download fetch), so the backstop holds; the gap is future drift, with the client fetch-spy test as primary proof.
recommended_fix: Extend the grep to also reject function imports from the real api layer (e.g. `import api/` lines in demo/ except the documented type-only api_error/auth_api imports in demo_api.gleam).

title: Baked Aoife PDF shows 'Co-applicants: 1' with no co-applicant detail
evidence: co_applicant_count: 1, ... snapshot: ApplicationSnapshot( application: p.row, co_applicants: [], income_sources: [], documents: [], ) ... #field-line("Co-applicants", str(app.co_applicant_count)) #if app.co_applicants.len() > 0 [ #v(3mm) #text(...)[Other adults moving in]
detail: row_aoife() sets co_applicant_count: 1 (the PR body touts the co-applicant story) but the pre-bake passes co_applicants: [], so the template prints the count line and skips the 'Other adults moving in' block. The shipped showcase PDF under-renders the co-applicant fixture story.
recommended_fix: If the co-applicant story matters in the PDF, populate snapshot.co_applicants for Aoife (the imported GetCoApplicantsByApplicationRow type is available); otherwise set co_applicant_count: 0 so the PDF doesn't claim a co-applicant it doesn't render.
